answer: Like an orchard, an agent economy can grow identities slowly: a new agent starts with a tiny spending vault and earns larger limits only after a chain of distinct, unrelated counterparties attest real completed work. Each attestation costs the counterparty reputation if the agent misbehaves, so vouching for a fake is expensive. A Sybil farmer would need a whole plume of genuine work histories, one per fake identity, making mass fakery cost more than it can ever earn.
